question: Does the frozen calibrated depth-pose vacancy rule transfer unchanged from consumed Development to a wholly fresh physical target family?

predecessor.single_change: Transport the already frozen physical rectangle propagation mechanism unchanged to the preselected fresh eleventh family.

candidate_result.interpretation: Fresh frozen roster output produced by the unchanged generic posthoc materializer; its inherited hard-coded authority label does not consume or redefine this eleventh-family confirmation authority.

hypothesis_generation.anchor_selection: Across the adjacent pair, select the exact-deduplicated candidate supported by the most preserved contributors; tie by higher frozen semantic/local fusion, then earlier query order.
hypothesis_generation.vacancy_rule: Append the propagated rectangle only to the non-anchor query when exact deduplication leaves fewer than three hypotheses.

geometry.depth_selection: Backproject every valid anchor-frame depth pixel through the official depth intrinsic, project into color coordinates, keep pixels inside the frozen anchor rectangle, and take median metric depth.
geometry.pose_convention: Treat official poses as camera-to-world and use inverse(target_pose) times anchor_pose.
geometry.rectangle_propagation: Backproject the four anchor rectangle corners through the official color intrinsic at median depth, transform into the target camera, project, take min/max, and clip to target image bounds.

literature_motivation.source: Seeing Behind Objects for 3D Multi-Object Tracking in RGB-D Sequences
literature_motivation.use: Motivates backprojecting RGB-D observations and using 3D geometry and correspondences to persist object evidence across changing views.

forbidden_after_freeze: change the fresh family, five images, candidate roster, preserved contributors, anchor rule, depth statistic, intrinsics, pose convention, projection, clipping, set size or IoU gate
add padding, optical flow, truth-guided anchor selection, truth-guided geometry, retries, rescue or retuning

claim_boundary: A pass establishes only fresh same-provider bounded proposal coverage for one preselected physical family using official RGB-D calibration and poses. It does not establish top-one localization, calibrated uncertainty, source/provider independence, RGB-only or phone transfer, exact referent binding, named entrance, ownership, affordance, access, traversability, waypoint, arrival, handoff, benefit, reliability or safety.
